observation.visible_scene: Against a black background, a hand holds an inverted squeeze bottle (white nozzle cap pointing down, red label partially visible) above a clear cylindrical glass filled with transparent water. A thin, continuous vertical stream of red liquid falls from the nozzle into the water, where a red dye cloud is forming and sinking. The hand, bottle, glass, and stream stay in fixed screen positions throughout, indicating a static camera and a steady pour.
visible_changes: The red plume inside the water grows larger and more diffuse over time, developing a wispy, billowing tail that sinks and spreads rather than translating as a solid object.
The thin red stream from nozzle to water surface remains essentially constant in position and continuity, with small scattered red specks/droplets hovering near it that persist across frames.
The hand and bottle show no noticeable movement; the water surface line and glass position remain unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the pouring began and whether it continues or stops after the last frame.
The final extent of dye mixing and whether the stream eventually breaks or the cloud fully disperses.
The exact identities of the liquids and the bottle contents.
uncertain_details: Camera is assumed static based on fixed object positions, but background is featureless so subtle motion cannot be fully ruled out.
The bottle label text is only partially legible.
Minor wobble of the stream and the precise motion of individual airborne droplets are hard to track frame to frame.
